author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Warwick police have charged a 55-year-old man with allegedly stealing an electric bicycle valued at $4,000, WJAR reported Monday.
The suspect, identified by police as Shane Mills, faces a charge of larceny over $1,500. Police said he was on probation at the time of his arrest.

The charge is an allegation, and the case will proceed through the Rhode Island court system. The initial report did not include additional details about where the e-bike was taken, how police identified the suspect or whether the bicycle was recovered.

E-bikes can carry significant value because of their batteries, motors and specialized components. Owners are encouraged to record serial numbers, use secure locks and keep purchase documentation in case a bicycle is stolen.
NorthEast News will update this story if court records or police provide more information about the allegation, the investigation or the status of the e-bike.
dek: Police say a 55-year-old Warwick man was charged with larceny after an e-bike valued at $4,000 was reported stolen.
headline: Warwick man charged in alleged $4,000 e-bike theft
